highlights_headline: SkiaSharp 4.156.0 improves platform compatibility, rendering reliability, and managed allocation behavior.
highlights_body: Apple targets now require newer operating systems, WebAssembly packages include their WebGPU implementation correctly, and common image and text-shaping paths allocate less memory.

breaking.title: iOS and tvOS now require version 14
breaking.body: The iOS and tvOS native assets and target framework metadata now require iOS 14.0 or tvOS 14.0. Update applications that support earlier operating-system versions or remain on a previous SkiaSharp release.

bullets.lead: Android texture rendering follows display refresh
bullets.detail: Android GL texture views synchronize rendering with the display refresh cycle for steadier presentation.

bullets.lead: Front-buffered streams no longer retain sources
bullets.detail: Front-buffered managed streams release their source stream when no longer needed.

bullets.lead: Image pixel copies allocate less managed memory
bullets.detail: Managed image pixel-copy operations avoid unnecessary allocations while preserving their output.

bullets.lead: Text shaping avoids temporary encoding allocations
bullets.detail: HarfBuzzSharp reuses buffers for UTF-32 text input and formats feature strings without native heap allocation.
iOS and tvOS packages now target version 14.0, and native macOS binaries require macOS 11.0.

bullets.lead: WebAssembly WebGPU builds package native support
bullets.detail: The WebGPU C++ implementation is included in the SkiaSharp native library so .NET WebAssembly applications do not compile it during their link step.

bullets.lead: Linux uses the bundled HarfBuzz symbols
bullets.detail: Native Linux builds bind HarfBuzz functionality from the bundled library rather than resolving it from the application environment.

contributor_summaries.VirgilMing: Bundled HarfBuzz symbol binding on Linux and more reliable Blazor CPU sample tests
